blocks.p: Before the sky was fully light, Rei read the chapter Gin had headed Symbols, Seals and Tattoos. Then he read the dictionary of glyphs that came after it. He read all of it, in order, the way Gin had asked to be read. He had watched his brother draw these shapes at the desk a hundred times and had never once asked what they were. Gin had noticed that too. He had written it down.

blocks.cap: Gin under the needle, Rei on the plastic stool

blocks.p: Halfway through the preface, Rei stopped and sat very still. Gin wrote that one late night, going down his left arm, he had twice come to a mark he did not remember having tattooed. Rei remembered both. He had been there both times, sitting on a plastic stool in a back room that smelled of antiseptic and green tea, watching the needle and pretending to read. Gin had blamed the late hour and the number of marks. Reading it now, in the month when Gin's handwriting leaned, Rei did not blame anything.

doc.title: Gin's book, Chapter Twenty-Two. Preface
lines: Written late, sleeves down. Rei made tea and I let it go cold, which he will mention in the morning, and be right to.

There is an obvious joke about the man covered shoulder to fingertip in configurations sitting down to write the chapter on why the disciplined ones stay clean. I am the joke. I may as well tell it first.

Cataloguing the body-seals for this chapter, I went down the left arm in order, the way I always have, and twice I reached a mark I did not remember sitting for. Both times Rei could tell me when and where, because he was there, because he is reliably the one who remembers the parts of my own life I misplace. I am putting it down to the number of them and the hour.
G.U. Keys on the hook. I counted them, which is new, and did not care for the fact that counting had started to feel necessary.

blocks.p: The next pages explained how the shapes worked. Gin wrote them like a teacher, plainly, as if he expected someone to learn from them one day. Rei understood now that the someone was him.

doc.title: How symbols work
lines: Symbols work because the knowledge behind them is real. Not faith, not belief. Specific geometric configurations interact with the membrane in documented and repeatable ways. A correctly drawn binding constrains entity movement whether or not the one who drew it believes it will work. The tool functions on precision, not intention. The veil is not mystical. It is real. We have incomplete models for it. Those are different problems.
Strength scales with the practitioner's Symbol Work and rank. The configuration is the same. The practitioner's veil depth decides how much of it actually executes.

Substrate. Standard ink on paper lasts hours. Specific inks on the right substrates last days. Carved configurations in the right materials last until damaged. Tattooed configurations are permanent and uncontrollable. Always active. No off switch.
Preparation. Ten minutes for a standard configuration, with materials. Anything rushed under three minutes is unreliable. I have never drawn one in a hurry that held the way it should.

Resistance. A standard binding holds a Class E demon indefinitely. Against Class B, contested every scene. Against Class A, contested every round of active pressure. No standard configuration permanently holds Class S. It buys time.

Noise. Quiet preparation makes none. Activation on entity contact makes a little. A rushed configuration pushed with active ability makes the most. This is why experienced people prepare before the situation asks.

blocks.p: Rei read the page slowly. It was simpler than it looked. A symbol was not a prayer. It was a shape, and the shape did the work, the way a key opens a lock whether or not the person turning it believes in keys. A practitioner's skill at drawing these shapes was called Symbol Work, and it was measured in levels. Ink on paper faded in hours. A tattoo never faded and never switched off. And the stronger the thing on the other side, the less time any shape could hold it.

doc.title: Tattoos. The Grid standard, and why the CVD stays clean
lines: You are not covered in a weekend. You are covered over years, one configuration at a time, each tested before the next goes under. I drew every line first in ink that washes off and wore it for a week. The hands come last. Done right, you read clean and you are anything but.

The CVD says it keeps practitioners unmarked because tattoos make assessment noisy. The true reason is institutional. A practitioner whose rank is partly masked by permanent ink is less controllable by the asset development pipeline. The CVD prefers readable people. The Grid inks because the one reaching for paper mid-encounter has already lost time.

Anti-possession. Reinforces membrane integrity at the skin. Raises the class needed for opportunistic possession by one. Does not stop a high-class demon prepared for that specific practitioner. Buys time. My first tattoo.
Rank mask. Reads one rank lower. Less effective than natural suppression, the Uedera technique. Side effect, you feel slightly more stable than you are.
Stability anchor. Slows depletion from one source chosen at tattooing. Only that one.
Binding, preloaded. On the forearm, always active at a low threshold. Fire it by pushing ability through the existing lines. Cheaper and with no preparation, against what it was designed for.

The ones on my hands, between the knuckles, are not spells. They are keys. Each is tied to a working seal inked on the trunk or arms, and a touch in the right place, in the right order, fires that seal without paper. I developed the keying myself. It is in no CVD training material. From across a room it looks like a man rubbing his hands, pressing his sternum, steepling his fingers. If you ever have to read me and cannot find the configurations, that is the point. They are on me, always, and the hands are how I reach them.

blocks.p: So that was what the marks on his brother's skin were. Rei had always thought of them as Gin's, the way a face is someone's. Now he saw that each one was a tool, chosen and tested and added over years. The small marks between Gin's knuckles were not decoration either. They were switches. When Gin rubbed his hands together or pressed a palm to his chest, he was firing a seal somewhere else on his body. Rei had seen him do it a thousand times and had thought it was a habit.

doc.title: Skin glyphs. The control problem
lines: Paper is off until you turn it on. An untrained skin glyph is always on. In a high-entity place it fires by itself. In a strong emotion it surges. A practitioner with an untrained Restraining Circle tattoo can trap himself inside his own field in a moment of distress. A Threshold Ward that fires in a panic blocks the entities it was made for and also cooperative spirits, communication glyphs and any practitioner with a strong signature. You are warded against the world.

Cascades. Two skin glyphs that work alone can wreck each other together. Anti-possession and Banishment on the same person fire at once in a possession event and produce neither, with full backlash from both. The Grid has documented eleven serious cascade incidents in the past eight years. Three needed Psychometabolic intervention.

A heavily tattooed practitioner walking a thin spot makes noise as if using abilities while doing nothing. A tattoo running passively for six hours in a contaminated area may fire at forty percent when you finally reach for it. Skin does not reset the way paper does. The slow version has a name in the Grid's medical notes. Configuration bleed. You feel slightly worse every morning and never find the cause.

Training. Symbol Work 3 to begin. A mentor who has trained his own. In the northern wards Tanizaki is one of four who can teach it. At least three months of practice per glyph, specific to that glyph. Exposure exercises, stress exercises, precision exercises at half strength. After the first, each one takes half the time. This is why sensible people get one, train it fully, then think about the next.
I left eighteen months between my first, anti-possession, and my second, the forearm binding. The exercises are in the year-three pages.
This happened to someone I know. The cascade took three months to stabilise. She is fine now. She would prefer I not say who she is.

blocks.p: Rei found the year-three pages. The exercises ran down the left margin in Gin's small print. Down the right margin, in the same pen, ran notes about Rei. R. maths test, did badly, did not care. R. did not eat lunch again. R. laughed at something on the train today and I did not ask what, and should have. The method was sound. The margin was the part Rei had to put the book down for.
He made more tea and let it go cold, the way Gin used to. Then he read on, to the page about what his brother carried every day.

doc.title: What I carry
lines: Six prepared configurations at any time. Three containment variants, chosen by the expected entity. One banishment. One communication, for the encounters where talking is right. One I developed in year four, a slow-acting disruption, which Grid contacts keep finding on me and asking about.
A standard set of threshold wards, folded in the left front pocket of every bag I own. I replace them weekly whether I used them or not.

The most powerful thing I carry is the exorcism circle, in five parts, sealed separately. I have used it once in six years. I prepared for three months before that operation. The preparation made the difference.

Prepare in advance. That is the only advice on symbol work that matters before you learn the rest. And learn from someone who knows them. Documentation makes configurations learnable. It does not make you able. Find a teacher first.

blocks.p: After that came the dictionary itself. A glyph, Gin explained, is a shape drawn on paper ahead of time, folded and carried until it is needed. All the real work goes into drawing it. Using it is only a touch.

blocks.cap: Glyphs drawn in advance, with time and a flat surface

doc.title: How glyphs work
lines: A glyph is ink on paper, drawn in advance with time, a flat surface and enough light. You fold it and carry it. Activation is immediate. Touch it, direct your intent, done. The cost is paid in the preparation, when the configuration forms in the veil layer. There is no way to tell a bad glyph from a good one by looking at it. You find out when you activate it.
The CVD registry lists three hundred and twelve standardised configurations, and that is the conservative count. The eighteen below are the ones I trust with my own hands.

A warning, because someone always tries. A configuration is a geometry and can be adapted. People who understand why a glyph works do this carefully. People who copy a shape and change it to suit themselves draw something that no longer does what they think. A glyph does not fail politely. It fires wrong, and it fires on the person who drew it.

Paper. Any paper works, a receipt, washi, a torn envelope. Size sets the scale. A business card gives the base effect. A5 gives base plus one. A4 gives base plus two, or doubles the duration, and doubles the preparation time. Folding does not reduce it. Every glyph is single use.

Floor. A circle drawn on a floor has no size limit. Each extra metre of radius adds one percent to the stability cost. A ten-metre floor exorcism circle costs base plus nine. A floor glyph cannot be reclaimed. Smudge it and it breaks without firing and the cost is paid for nothing. Tanizaki's floor still shows the chalk ghosts of the same circles drawn and redrawn for years.
Carrying. More than ten prepared glyphs on one person can be felt by a Clairsentient at Level 5. More than fifteen and anyone in range feels them. Carry what the operation needs.

blocks.p: Each entry in the lists that followed gave the glyph's name in English and in Japanese characters, then how long it took to draw, then what it did, then the level of Symbol Work needed to draw it. Gin had split them into groups. The first twelve protected and contained. The next six did harm. And the last few, at the very bottom of the chapter, he did not recommend at all.

doc.title: The twelve configurations
lines: 1. Restraining Circle 拘束陣 · 15 min · A 3 m field. Entities inside when it fires cannot leave under their own will for two hours. Class B contests it every round. Practitioners walk through freely. Symbol Work 3.

2. Threshold Ward 閾守印 · 10 min · Pressed across a doorframe or sill. Spirits, suffering beings and Class E demons cannot cross. Class B crosses at a cost and arrives shaken. 24 hours. One per entry point. The most portable. Symbol Work 2.
3. Silence Mark 沈黙符 · 5 min · Pressed to the forearm or collar. Hides your passive signature for 2 hours. Using an ability under it stands out more, not less. Symbol Work 2.

4. Anchor Seal 錨封 · 20 min · Holds an anchored spirit within 10 m in place for an hour and makes it more visible. Meant to keep a conversation partner from leaving. The fold is part of it. Symbol Work 3.

5. Banishment Glyph 退魔文 · 30 min · Sealed in an envelope, fired by tearing. A 5 m pulse. Spirits sent veil-side for 1 to 6 hours. Suffering beings weakened for a day. Carry no more than two. Symbol Work 3.
6. Stability Mark 安定符 · 5 min · Pressed to the inside of the wrist. Your stability cannot fall below a quarter for one scene. Can be made for someone else, on their skin, at your cost. Symbol Work 2.

7. Alert Seal 感知文 · 5 min · Any surface. When an entity crosses within 5 m you feel it up to 500 m away, most say as pressure behind the eyes. 8 hours. The most cost-efficient of the twelve. Symbol Work 1.

8. Purification Seal 浄化印 · 45 min for a set of three · Placed at three corners within thirty seconds. Clears register contamination and blocks new contamination for 72 hours. All three from one session. Symbol Work 3.

9. Communication Glyph 通言文 · 10 min · Unfolded on a flat surface. Lets one entity within 20 m speak in human-accessible form without Telepathy. Spirits use it fluently. Class B demons will use it if they want to, so be careful what you say. Symbol Work 2.
10. Iron Wall 鉄壁 · 10 min, on iron-powder paper · Slapped against a hard surface. A barrier for one scene or three strikes. Stops the first telekinetic blow outright. Symbol Work 2.

11. Suppression Mark 隠符 · 5 min · Pressed to skin. Your readable rank drops two levels for four hours. Vanguard reads as Channel. Channel reads as Sensitive. One hour if you fight. Does not stack with suppression training. Symbol Work 2.

12. Exorcism Circle 除霊陣 · 1 to 2 hours, never under 60 minutes · Four outer glyphs and a centre mark, made as one set in one session, the centre drawn last. Placed at the compass points around the host. It fires when all five touch the floor. The entity cannot jump to a new host. It must go deeper or leave through the open top of the circle. The host surfaces longer and more often. The definitive possession recovery configuration. Symbol Work 4. I prepared three complete sets. Two are in the archive's bottom drawer, sealed in washi.

doc.title: The six that do harm. 'The geometry is the instruction.'
lines: 13. The Severance 断絶 · 20 min · Pressed on the anchor, never the entity. A vertical line cut by a horizontal, two arcs that do not meet. Cuts a spirit from what holds it. For a demon in a host, severs its main grip for a few moments, when exorcism is easiest. You feel the cut too. Have your grounding object ready. Symbol Work 3.
14. The Weight 重圧 · 15 min · Dropped on the floor. Five circles sharing one bottom point, the innermost filled. The entity is that centre. Its presence drops by two for the scene. Symbol Work 2.

15. The Mirror 鏡反 · 25 min · Held facing the entity, then released. Two triangles, one inverted, six lines to six points. What the entity broadcasts comes back to it. A demon managing its face is readable as it really is for a moment, and a Class B demon's social engineering fails. Anyone in range sees through the presentation. You also feel your own broadcast reflected. Symbol Work 3.

16. The Threshold Burn 閾焔 · 20 min · Six flames under a line, not quite touching. Does not block. Lets the entity cross and then burns it. Once per entity. You sleep a little worse while you carry it. Symbol Work 2.

17. The Arrest 制止 · 30 min · Four capped lines meeting at a filled centre inside a circle. Pressed against the entity or its surface. Freezes it, Class B for less time. Does not harm. Completely stops. You freeze too, for half a second. Be ready to take a hit. Symbol Work 4.

18. The Corrosion 腐食 · 40 min, cedar ash in the ink · A worn circle around a spiral that never reaches the centre. Placed in the anchor space. Wears the entity down a little at the end of each scene for three scenes. Preparing it feels like melancholy. Symbol Work 3.

doc.title: Two I will not recommend
lines: The eighteen above I have tested and I stand by. These last two I document because the archive should be honest, not because you should ever draw them. One ends you. The other decides for you where you go. I have drawn the first twice, for others who asked, and never the second.
If you are reading this far down the chapter you are either very thorough or in real trouble. If it is the second, think once more before the ink is dry. G.U.

19. The Final Refusal 自決 · 90 min, in your own blood, by a master of the form · A self closed and struck through, a mouth sealed and the thing inside it burned, a door drawn shut over the body, ringed in locks. Pressed over the heart and finished by your own hand. The seal is not finished until you finish it. It ends you instantly and burns what an enemy wanted. No Telepath can read a secret from the body. A possessing entity is refused the host. It cannot be used on anyone but yourself. A wrong stroke makes it inert, which is its own danger if you were counting on it. There is no backlash. There is only the cost, which is everything. I have drawn it correctly twice, both times for others who asked, both times burned unused. I do not write about those nights.

20. The Scatter 散転 · 20 min · Crushed in the fist. A single point throwing lines out in every direction, none chosen. The veil throws you somewhere within roughly fifty to three hundred metres, direction and distance not yours. You will not be where the threat is. You may be somewhere worse. It costs ten stability, and if you land below fifteen percent, whatever is waiting where you land may try for you. Use it to not die here. Accept that you have chosen nothing else.

21. Custom configuration · Not fixed. The practitioner's own geometry, adapted from one of the above or built new by someone who understands why a glyph works. Improvise only if you can predict the backlash. A glyph drawn wrong fires on the one who drew it.

blocks.p: Rei read the entry for the Final Refusal twice. He did not want to know which two people had asked his brother to draw it, or why. He turned the page quickly. Stuck inside the back cover of the chapter was a yellow post-it note.

doc.title: Post-it, inside the back cover of the chapter
lines: Studying this gives understanding. It does not give the hand. R. will need someone to show him. Tanizaki for the standard set, Banishment, the Exorcism Circle, the Weight and the Arrest. Shimizu for the Burn. Kurosawa knows the offensive ones and will not volunteer it.

blocks.p: Under the post-it there was one more page. It was dated only by the day of the week, like most of Gin's personal notes, and it was about paper.

blocks.cap: A washi shop in Kanda, where Gin bought his paper

doc.title: End of Chapter Twenty-Two. Personal note
lines: A Monday. The paper from Kanda is on the desk. Forty sheets of washi, the kind the Grid contact recommended. I prepared six configurations this morning before I wrote anything. Threshold ward, binding, banishment, the custom disruption, two communication variants. The hand moves. The configuration emerges.
Rei walked past while I was working and looked at the paper without asking what it was. He already knows. He has started to know what the preparations mean without knowing that he knows.
G.U. Keys on the hook. The washi will outlast the need for it. I prepared more than I will use. I do not know why I did that today specifically.

blocks.p: Rei closed the book. He went to the desk and opened the bottom drawer. Two bundles of washi lay there, each tied with plain cord, each marked in Gin's hand with a small compass rose. Rei thought of the Exorcism Circle, its glyphs laid out at the compass points around the host. Rei did not untie them. He laid his palm flat on the top one and felt, under the paper, the faint, patient hum of something drawn correctly a long time ago by someone who had expected to need it. Then he shut the drawer and went to find his shoes. He could not draw a single one of these shapes. But Gin had already drawn them, and a prepared glyph does not care whose hand releases it.
